title: Carpet Bag Steak
description: Scotch fillet stuffed with fresh oysters and Camembert cheese, finished with a red wine and demi glace sauce. The most theatrical dish on the menu.

ingredients.notes: Don't add too much all at once — you can't take it out once it's in.

method.instruction: Cut a deep horizontal pocket in each scotch fillet, being careful not to pierce through the other side.
Stuff each pocket with 3 oysters and slices of Camembert. Secure the opening with toothpicks.

Season the outside with salt and pepper. Pan-fry in a hot skillet for 3–4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. The Camembert will melt inside. Remove steaks and rest on a warm plate.
In the same pan, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced shallot and cook until softened, about 1–2 minutes.
Deglaze with red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce by half, about 1–2 minutes.
Add demi glace and any reserved oyster liquor. Simmer until the sauce is glossy and coats the back of a spoon, about 2–3 minutes.
Remove toothpicks from steaks. Plate and spoon the red wine demi glace sauce generously over the top.
Add salt and pepper to season

notes.title: The Magic Inside
notes.content: The Camembert melts into the oysters inside the steak while cooking — that is the signature of this dish. The cheese and oysters fuse together, creating a rich, briny, creamy centre.

notes.title: Wine Choice
notes.content: Use a full-bodied red wine like Shiraz or Cabernet Sauvignon for deglazing. Avoid light reds — they won't stand up to the demi glace and beef.

notes.title: Oyster Liquor
notes.content: Reserve the oyster liquor and add it to the sauce. It adds a subtle brininess that ties the surf and turf elements together beautifully.
